races.name: Joe Mac's Big Retirement Bash Handicap Stakes (GBBPlus Race)
Jordan Electrics EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (For Horses In Bands A, B, C And D) (EBF Restricted Qualifier) (GBB Race)
Hamish MacGregor Memorial Nursery

runners_data.name: Fern Clyde
runners_data.note: Lone confirmed pace-setter with excellent course-applicable form — four of five recent runs on good ground produced a win and three places; races prominently with headgear (ht) noted, and Tim Easterby's juveniles tend to show up well fresh; the style-fit tag is marginal here given she is likely to actually secure her preferred lead in this small field.

runners_data.name: Brandenburg
runners_data.note: Has won over 5f on soft and placed over 6f on good, giving her solid ground-trip credentials for David Egan aboard; a natural prominent runner who is pushed back to midfield on the map only because this field's pace order is already crowded at the front — she will seek a position closer to the pace than the map implies.

runners_data.name: Quiet Soul
runners_data.note: Michael Dods juvenile that has shown progressive form — second twice and third once in five runs — but as a genuine hold-up type she needs the pace to fold, which is an unlikely gift in a race Fern Clyde is set to control; 35 days off is worth monitoring though Dods typically has his horses ready.

runners_data.name: Beauty For Love
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's representative has recent 6f experience and a placed run on soft ground, but her hold-up style is the most difficult to deploy in a small field where the front-runner is unchallenged; at OR 73 she has the rating to compete but the race shape is working against her profile from flag-fall.

runners_data.name: Tango Hotel
runners_data.note: One-day turnaround for George Scott's 2-year-old is an immediate flag — runners returning this quickly are worth querying for wellbeing even if fit; has a win on soft and placed on good, and will want to race prominently, likely pushing for a position just behind Fern Clyde with Tudhope steering; headgear noted (p) and keen early running is possible.

races.paceDynamic: Fern Clyde is the lone confirmed front-runner here and, with only Tango Hotel and Brandenburg as prominent-types in a five-runner field, she is almost certain to lead unchallenged from the gates over this 6f Hamilton straight. The pace she sets is likely to be controlled and sustainable rather than scorching — no rival is likely to take her on — which typically favours the horse on the front end at this course, where Hamilton's stiff finish can expose those coming from behind. Quiet Soul and Beauty For Love sit in hold-up positions and will need the pace to collapse in front of them, which is unlikely with Fern Clyde dictating comfortably. The race shape clearly favours prominent or front-running profiles: a steady, uncontested lead over a stiff 6f rewards whoever can dominate the early fractions and sustain them. This field holds more prominent-running types than the pace map can accommodate in their natural position — Brandenburg and Tango Hotel both want to race prominently, and Fern Clyde is most likely to secure the actual lead with the others forced to slot in behind.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Fern Clyde Controls Easily
scenarios.trigger: If Fern Clyde gets a clean break and dictates an uncontested, honest gallop to the line.
scenarios.body: Fern Clyde sets the fractions from the front and, with no credible challenger for the lead, arrives at the stiff Hamilton finish with reserves intact; her good-ground form (4/5 similar-going runs finishing first or placed) supports this shape strongly.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Grind It Out
scenarios.trigger: If Tango Hotel or Brandenburg press Fern Clyde early and turn the race into a sustained battle for position between the prominent runners.
scenarios.body: The pace quickens from the outset with Tango Hotel (1-day turnaround noted, fresh, likely to race keenly) pushing Fern Clyde along, and the winner emerges from the horses best able to handle a stronger gallop over 6f; this marginally opens the door for a closer.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Swoop Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is unexpectedly strong and the front runners tie each other up, leaving Quiet Soul or Beauty For Love with a wall of beaten horses to pick off.
scenarios.body: Quiet Soul's step up to 6f from 5f looks workable given her placed form on good ground, and Beauty For Love has the most recent experience at this trip; however, both require a tempo that this small, pace-light field may simply never generate.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Chaos Scrambles Field
scenarios.trigger: If a slow or uneven start reshuffles positions and denies Fern Clyde the lead, forcing her to race out of role.
scenarios.body: With only five runners and small-field dynamics, a stumble or check out of the gates could compress the field and nullify the expected pace shape entirely; the beneficiary in this scenario would most likely be whichever prominent type gets the cleanest early passage.

watchPoints.text: Tango Hotel returns just one day after her last run — watch her in the paddock and at the start for any signs of residual fatigue or undue keenness that could compromise her.

Brandenburg and Tango Hotel both want to be prominent and will test whether Fern Clyde can hold them off cleanly out of the gates — a scrappy early exchange could disrupt the expected controlled lead shape.

Quiet Soul and Beauty For Love are genuine hold-up types in a five-runner field with a strong front-runner — watch whether they can find clear daylight in the straight or get trapped in a small group with nowhere to go.
Fern Clyde's headgear (ht) is worth noting at the start — any reluctance to stride on smoothly from the gates would be the key signal that the dominant pace scenario is unravelling.

races.name: Hamish Macgregor Memorial Nursery Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Ferrous
runners_data.note: Has place form over this C&D trip on similar ground but recent form is patchy (three sixth-place finishes in last four), and as a hold-up type for Jack Channon will need something to go wrong for others to get involved late at Hamilton.

runners_data.name: Commanche Falls
runners_data.note: Returns from a lengthy 148-day absence with headgear fitted, but his main role here is pace-setter — ten runs in similar going suggest he stays competitive at this level, and if fit enough to quicken at the 2f pole he becomes a serious factor, not merely a pacemaker.

runners_data.name: Jordan Electrics
runners_data.note: Consistent finisher for Jim Goldie who genuinely wants to race off a strong pace from behind, but with the field stacked with prominent types he is unlikely to find the searching early gallop he needs; his tendency to fade in the finish is an additional concern.

runners_data.name: Manila Scouse
runners_data.note: Won over this exact C&D trip in his most recent start and holds strong course-and-distance form with two wins and four places in similar going — naturally wants to race prominently but faces stiff competition for that berth, which may compromise his rhythm if shuffled further back than ideal.

runners_data.name: Sir Garfield
runners_data.note: Has won two of his last five starts on good ground and clearly comes into this in form, but as a horse who races prominently by nature he is one of several fighting for the same space; his best chance depends on finding a clear run off the heels of the leaders.

runners_data.name: Gangsta Man
runners_data.note: Three wins in similar going give him strong pace-shape credentials, and Paul Mulrennan's booking is a significant plus — of all the prominent types in this field he looks best placed to secure a genuine second or third spot and use it to strike from the front two furlongs out.

runners_data.name: Strike Red
runners_data.note: Winner over this trip on good ground with recent placed form at the track — Billy Garritty keeps the ride and this horse has the class to go with the early pace; his inconsistency over the last six runs (including a 17th) is a note of caution.

runners_data.name: Saint Lawrence
runners_data.note: Kevin Stott partner for Kevin Ryan, placed in similar going but that was a one-off in otherwise modest recent form; as a hold-up type returning from 41 days off he needs a generous pace and a clear run, neither of which looks guaranteed in this shape.

races.paceDynamic: Commanche Falls is the lone confirmed front-runner and, returning from 148 days off, will likely set a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front without being genuinely pressured at any stage. Gangsta, Strike Red, and the natural prominent types make up a sizeable group who want to race close to the pace, but with Sir Garfield, Manila Scouse, and Jordan Electrics all being genuine prominent or hold-up types redistributed to midfield on the map, this field carries more pace-seeking horses than the shape can comfortably accommodate — Gangsta Man and Strike Red are best placed to actually secure prominent spots behind Commanche Falls, while Sir Garfield and Manila Scouse are most likely to be squeezed wider or further back than ideal. With one horse able to dictate at a measured tempo over 6f on good turf at Hamilton, the race shape strongly favours horses who can travel just off the pace in second or third — prominent racers with tactical speed — rather than true hold-up types who need a strong early gallop to generate momentum from the rear.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Front Sets Up Midfield
scenarios.trigger: If Commanche Falls leads at a steady tempo and no rival is able to seriously contest early, setting up a race where those travelling prominently just behind have first run.
scenarios.body: Commanche Falls dictates throughout without pressure, and horses sitting second or third early conserve energy before striking in the final 2f; Hamilton's undulations reward those with tactical speed and a turn of foot rather than pure closers.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Hold-Up Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Commanche Falls or the prominent group go faster than expected and tie each other up, leaving a vacuum for a late finisher to pick up the pieces.
scenarios.body: A contested gallop burns off the leaders in the final furlong, giving Ferrous or Saint Lawrence the momentum to close; hold-up horses benefit from rivals burning out, but Hamilton's track generally resists pure late swoops and true closers are not plentiful here.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Sticks On
scenarios.trigger: If Commanche Falls, fresher than expected after 148 days off, quickens clear at the 2f pole and the field fails to close on a controlled gallop.
scenarios.body: With no rival applying early pressure, Commanche Falls simply stretches the field at will and the prominent horses never get close enough to challenge; a fit, well-handicapped front-runner dictating its own fractions on good ground is hard to reel in.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Scrimmage Shuffles Field
scenarios.trigger: If the congestion among the numerous pace-seeking horses causes bumping or checking early, radically reshuffling positions and creating a chaotic tempo.
scenarios.body: Horses caught in traffic or knocked out of stride lose ground they cannot recover on a 6f flat track, and any runner who finds a clean passage despite the chaos takes advantage; this scenario is unlikely given the modest pace likely to be set but cannot be ruled out entirely.

watchPoints.text: Gangsta Man's ability to actually secure a prominent berth directly behind Commanche Falls will be decisive — if he gets a clean run in second or third, he is the primary danger in the dominant scenario.

Commanche Falls' fitness after 148 days off is the single biggest uncertainty in this race — if he ties up early rather than quickening, the entire pace shape collapses and the scenarios shift markedly toward closers.

Sir Garfield and Manila Scouse are both natural front-runners who may clash for position in the first furlong, creating bumping or checking that knocks them out of their preferred rhythm and potentially benefits horses drawn or jumping wider.

Jordan Electrics has a noted tendency to fade in the finish — if he is squeezed for room early and has to use energy to find a position he would not naturally take, his chance of landing a blow in the final furlong is materially reduced.

Saint Lawrence is 41 days fresh and has only five runs in similar going — watch the market for any late support that might indicate he has been sharpened for this return, as his hold-up profile would suit a breakneck pace that is not expected here.

races.name: Jordan Electrics Scottish Stewards' Cup Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Mr Colonel
runners_data.note: Shane Gray's hold-up mount has the most upside if the gallop is truly strong — a winner at 10f on Good going (1/10f/GOO) and placed on soft, with solid similar-going form (5/6 runs), but 1m3f in a race not expected to be strongly run means the late challenge may never fully materialise; 30 days since last run is not a concern for the Fahey yard.

runners_data.name: Superior Choice
runners_data.note: John & Thady Gosden's 3yo has excellent winning form at up to 10f on Good ground (two wins from three similar-going runs), but as a natural front-runner pushed back to midfield by the race's pace configuration, he races in a position that does not suit — discount accordingly despite the quality of his recent form.

runners_data.name: Flawless Fusion
runners_data.note: Jessica Bedi's charge has modest similar-going form (0W0P from two comparable runs) and heads here on 46 days off; naturally a front-end runner who will be forced to race further back than preferred, and the headgear flag (hg:h) suggests she has needed encouragement before — an uphill task against stronger rivals from an unfavourable berth.

runners_data.name: Folk Pageant
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's yard is the busiest in the field (T14: 8/67) and Hart has a clear tactical brief — sit second to Prizeland and pounce. Two recent wins at 10f on Good and Soft ground, with six runs at 10f+ giving him genuine stamina credentials over this Hamilton 1m3f; the 7-day turnaround is not unusual for Johnston runners in form.

runners_data.name: Plaid
runners_data.note: James Fanshawe's 3yo carries solid form at 8-10f (two wins from five similar-going runs) and Daniel Muscutt is an experienced handler of positional races, but the horse's natural inclination to race prominently is frustrated by this field's configuration — operating 40 days fresh, he needs to overcome the tactical disadvantage of a midfield map position before he can express his best form.

runners_data.name: Prizeland
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's yard is firing (T14: 11/56) and PJ McDonald will exploit the lone front-running role with intelligence — two wins at 12f on Flat tracks (1/12f/STA) underpin the stamina for this trip and he has shown tactical versatility across Good and Soft. The [STYLE_FIT=0.90] flag reflects the fact that leading is his secondary mode, but in this field he will lead unchallenged and that changes the calculus entirely.

races.paceDynamic: Prizeland is the one confirmed front runner and, with no genuine challenger disputing the lead from the off over 1m3f at Hamilton, PJ McDonald can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front. Folk Pageant is the likeliest horse to press Prizeland from a prominent position, with Jason Hart likely to tuck in just behind the pace rather than force a duel. This field holds more prominent-leaning types than can all find their natural position — Plaid, Superior Choice, and Flawless Fusion are genuine front-to-midfield horses who will be shuffled back into unfamiliar midfield roles, compromising their ability to produce their best. The race shape — a steady-to-honest pace set by one horse largely uncontested — strongly favours either the pace-setter itself to control and outstay the field, or a close-tracking prominent racer (Folk Pageant) who can travel on the heels of the leader and pounce; hold-up types like Mr Colonel face the sternest task unless the pace genuinely stretches the field in the home straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prizeland Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Prizeland is allowed to stride clear from the gates and sets a measured, uncontested pace throughout the 1m3f trip.
scenarios.body: McDonald dictates every yard on a lone leader with no rival willing to put him under pressure, arriving at the straight full of running and quickening clear. A flat Hamilton track at a steady pace suits a horse with two wins at 1m2f+ on similar ground, and the Balding yard are in fine form (T14: 11/56).

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Close Tracker Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Folk Pageant tracks Prizeland closely through the race and produces a superior turn of foot in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Jason Hart, an astute reader of pace, keeps Folk Pageant within a length of Prizeland throughout, then asks for a decisive effort entering the home straight. Folk Pageant has won at 1m2f on Good twice in recent form (form: 911106 conceals a very sharp spell) and Charlie Johnston's yard is operating at 12% strike rate over 14 days.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Runners Find Gap
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or Prizeland sets a truly pedestrian gallop that compresses the field and allows redistributed midfield types to find their stride late.
scenarios.body: Plaid or Superior Choice, both natural prominent types forced back, manage to recover enough ground if the tempo is slow enough to have left a sprint finish in their legs. Both have strong winning form at this sort of trip on Good ground, but their chances are materially discounted because they are racing out of their natural position.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to string out the field and Mr Colonel can deliver one sustained late charge from off the pace.
scenarios.body: Mr Colonel has winning form on Good ground at 1m2f and posted his most recent win at 10f, but at 1m3f in a race not expected to be run at a truly searching gallop, the hold-up fractions may never truly suit. Shane Gray would need the front two to set a pace that burns them out, which the current dynamics make unlikely.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether any of Plaid, Superior Choice, or Flawless Fusion attempt to press Prizeland early — if two or more fight for the front, the pace dynamic shifts sharply and transforms this into a scenario that suits Mr Colonel far more than the map currently suggests.

Folk Pageant's 7-day turnaround and recent form string (911106) should be checked for whether that most recent run was a blow-out or a genuine effort — if the last run was a pipe-opener, Hart may be instructed to ride more aggressively than the pace map assumes.

Prizeland's [STYLE_FIT=0.90] tag is worth noting — if McDonald is instructed to track rather than lead, the entire race shape collapses and no single runner has the pace profile to fill the vacuum cleanly.

Mr Colonel is the only true hold-up horse in the field and may get a clean run wide on the track if the rest bunch behind the leader; watch his position at the 3f pole — if he's within three lengths of the pace at that stage, his late surge becomes meaningful.

Superior Choice's Gosden connections may instruct Foley to push forward regardless of competition — watch the early furlongs to see if the redistributed prominent types actually accept midfield or attempt to recover their natural positions, which would create a false pace.

races.name: Hamilton Park Celebrates 100 Years Of Racing Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Law Of Average
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins at five furlongs on good ground make his course-distance form compelling, and Chelsea Banham's yard is 3/7 over 14 days; a genuine hold-up type who will need Rock Of England to tie up to get competitive in a race where the pace is unlikely to be strong enough to set up a late surge.

runners_data.name: Justmyluck
runners_data.note: Returns from a 55-day break for Linda Perratt, whose strike rate is 0/12 over the past fortnight — a concern — and the headgear (hood) may sharpen her up, though similar-going figures of just 2 wins from 8 runs and the freshness make this a watch-and-see proposition for a horse that needs things to fall right.

runners_data.name: Jm Jhingree
runners_data.note: Won at five furlongs on good ground on his second-most recent start and is lightly weighted at OR 66, but his natural instinct is to come from the back of the field; placed in midfield on the map only because the rear of this small field is already taken, he is unlikely to secure any meaningful forward position in practice, which materially handicaps his chance.

runners_data.name: Rock Of England
runners_data.note: The race's lone front-runner, boasting a strong record at five furlongs on good ground — 11 placings from 15 starts at similar going — and Jason Hart takes the ride for Paul Midgley's yard; his STYLE_FIT flag acknowledges he may drift slightly off his natural lead, but in a field of five with no rival willing to push him, he should control the tempo regardless.

runners_data.name: Woohoo
runners_data.note: Paul Mulrennan partners a mare who has finished in the first two at five furlongs on good ground in four of her last five starts at similar going — a figure (13/15) that stands out as the best in this field; prominent by nature, she is perfectly positioned to track Rock Of England and is the most obvious beneficiary of this race shape regardless of which of the two prominent horses ultimately leads.

races.paceDynamic: Rock Of England is the lone confirmed front-runner in this five-runner field and should have things largely his own way from the gates, setting a measured, uncontested gallop over the five furlongs at Hamilton. Woohoo will press prominently just off the pace, providing some company but unlikely to apply the kind of sustained pressure that would destabilise Rock Of England's rhythm. The two hold-up horses, Law Of Average and Justmyluck, will need to close from the rear, while Jm Jhingree — a genuine hold-up type redistributed to midfield on the map because the rear is already occupied — is unlikely to secure a truly prominent pitch in practice. With a single pace-setter controlling tempo, this race shape strongly favours runners who can track the leader through the race and sustain their effort into the Hamilton finish, giving prominent racers and handy closers the clearest route, while pure hold-up horses face the biggest ask with limited cover and a steady rather than searching pace to close into.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Rock Of England Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Rock Of England jumps cleanly and dictates an uncontested, measured pace from the front.
scenarios.body: Rock Of England, a proven front-runner at five furlongs on good ground, sets his own terms and turns the contest into a test of stamina for those giving him a start; Woohoo, tracking throughout, is ideally positioned to challenge late and makes the most of sitting in the slipstream.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is quicker than expected and Rock Of England ties up inside the final furlong, leaving a gap for closers.
scenarios.body: Law Of Average, with back-to-back wins at five furlongs on good ground, has the form to pick up a tiring leader if the tempo proves stronger than anticipated; Justmyluck, returning from 55 days off, would need to produce a career-best but has course-distance form to theoretically threaten.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Woohoo presses Rock Of England harder than expected and outlasts him in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: Woohoo has exceptional course-and-distance form on good ground — the best in the field — and if she can push Rock Of England into an honest gallop, her finishing power could prove superior; her trainer Jim Goldie's five wins from 58 over 14 days suggests the horse is in working order.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Racer Lands It
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses late, creating an unusual scenario where Jm Jhingree, racing outside his natural hold-up role, benefits from a forward pitch.
scenarios.body: Jm Jhingree is a genuine hold-up type pushed into a mapped midfield position only because the true rear is congested, so this scenario demands he races atypically and the pace scenario falls perfectly; his recent win at five furlongs on good ground gives him a residual chance if everything goes his way, but this is the least likely shape.

watchPoints.text: Watch Rock Of England's early stride — if he jumps cleanly and goes unchallenged, he could dictate the entire race and prove very hard to catch, making his opening price crucial.

Woohoo's course-and-distance record on good ground (4W8P from 13 runs) is exceptional and she could easily dominate this scenario; any drifting in the market for her would be a significant red flag given the pace shape suits her perfectly.

Law Of Average is the most dangerous hold-up horse if the tempo quickens unexpectedly — she has won twice at this trip on identical going and Joey Haynes will be timing his challenge carefully from the rear.

Justmyluck's 55-day absence for Linda Perratt's yard, whose 14-day record stands at 0/12, means fitness is a genuine question mark; the hood may help on reappearance but she would need everything to go perfectly to land this from off the pace.

Jm Jhingree runs just four days after his last outing, but his redistribution from hold-up to mapped midfield masks the reality that he will likely race further back than his map position suggests — do not expect him to feature prominently in the finish unless the race completely falls apart in front of him.

races.name: Hampton By Hilton Hamilton Park Fillies' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Geo
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse with a solid good-ground record (sim-going 13/15, 1W3P) and has shown her best form at 8-11f, though she is being mapped to midfield here because this field's rear is crowded with true closers — Paul Mulrennan will need to find space early and she may not get the clean rails run she requires.|

runners_data.name: Sogniamo
runners_data.note: Daniel Tudhope takes the ride for David O'Meara, and her sole win came over 9f on good ground which sets this trip and going up well; she drops back from three hold-up rivals for the same ground at the rear, making her the most naturally placed closer in the field on pure style grounds.|

runners_data.name: Zermatt Star
runners_data.note: Tony Coyle & Kaine Wood send out a filly who has not placed on good ground in four attempts (sim-going 0W0P from 2), and 67 days off the track combined with a form string reading 6-5-0-0 in recent runs raises fitness and confidence questions; she is a hold-up type who needs things to fall perfectly.|

runners_data.name: Second Fiddle
runners_data.note: Iain Jardine's seven-year-old is the only prominent runner in the field, which gives Cara Tuke (claimer, 7lb) a straightforward tactical brief — sit behind Stella Lucente and track every move; her recent good-ground form (2nd and 3rd from 5 runs on similar going) makes her the most dangerous single beneficiary if Stella Lucente weakens.|

runners_data.name: Stella Lucente
runners_data.note: Jack Morland's three-year-old wears a hood and is the lone confirmed front-runner, giving Callum Rodriguez total control of the pace over this mile-and-a-half on good turf; she has been placed in five consecutive starts and ran on good ground once (2nd, 7f), so the combination of uncontested lead and step up to a staying trip may finally bring out a win, though she has yet to break her maiden.|

races.paceDynamic: Stella Lucente is the sole confirmed front-runner in this five-runner field and, facing no genuine challenger for the lead, she will set an uncomplicated, controlled tempo over the mile and a half on good ground at Hamilton. Second Fiddle is the only prominent-style runner and will likely slot in directly behind Stella Lucente, meaning the pace is entirely at Stella Lucente's discretion — she can dictate every stride without pressure. Geo, Sogniamo, and Zermatt Star are all hold-up types by nature, though Geo has been redistributed to midfield on the map because this field carries more hold-up horses than the rear of the field can accommodate — Sogniamo and Zermatt Star are more likely to settle furthest back, with Geo potentially pushed closer than ideal. A solo leader setting a comfortable, uncontested gallop over a staying trip strongly favours the prominent-to-lead profile: horses who travel close to the pace without expending energy in early scrimmaging are best placed to capitalise when that front-runner eventually tires or kicks, making Second Fiddle's proximity to Stella Lucente a significant tactical asset.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Stella Lucente Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Stella Lucente bowls along in front at a comfortable pace and the hold-up brigade cannot generate momentum from off the pace.
scenarios.body: Stella Lucente sets every fraction on her own terms, and without a rival to force her hoof, she can conserve enough for a sustained run to the line; her five consecutive placed efforts suggest she handles this pressure well.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Poacher Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Stella Lucente's pace is just slow enough to produce a false finish and Second Fiddle times a late thrust from second.
scenarios.body: Second Fiddle, travelling on the heels of Stella Lucente throughout, inherits the lead as the front-runner empties inside the final furlong; her recent form at 8-9f on good shows she can find a solid late effort when delivered at the right moment.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If Stella Lucente sets enough of a genuine gallop that the closer types get a meaningful target and generate a sustained finish from the rear.
scenarios.body: Sogniamo or Geo, settling well off the pace, finds the straight conditions ideal for a sweeping late run if the tempo has been honest; Sogniamo's course-going profile (1W1P from 3 on similar ground) gives her the best hold-up credentials here, while Geo's redistribution to midfield means she is racing outside her comfort zone and may not get the clean passage a true late-finisher needs.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Blanket Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Stella Lucente idles badly in front and the whole field converges in the final furlong for a chaotic driving finish.
scenarios.body: With only five runners the field would bunch tightly, and any horse travelling with momentum into the straight — including Zermatt Star who has shown form at this trip — could grab a share; Zermatt Star's lack of winning form and poor recent figures make this a low-percentage outcome regardless.

watchPoints.text: Watch Stella Lucente's early sections — if Callum Rodriguez elects to dawdle to an extreme on the lead, Second Fiddle's jockey Cara Tuke may be tempted to commit earlier than planned, which would dramatically change the shape of the race.

Geo is a genuine hold-up horse placed on the map closer to midfield due to field composition — if Paul Mulrennan cannot settle her in a comfortable position early, she may race too freely and find nothing late when it matters.

Sogniamo's fitness is worth checking: 28 days since her last run is fine, but she has only three career starts and a notable drop in form figures (8-1-8) — if she is not switched off cleanly by Tudhope, her stamina over a mile and a half on this step up in trip is unproven.

Zermatt Star has gone 67 days without a run and has zero placings on good ground from four attempts — monitor early to see whether Jason Hart elects to ride her handily rather than from her natural hold-up berth, which would be a stable-confidence signal worth noting.
